data_fields.name: pile_density_per_400_tiles
data_fields.donor_constant: count = zone tiles x density / 400 per tier (density values in zone JSON, not read)

data_fields.name: treasure_tier_min_max_units
data_fields.donor_constant: target pile value random in [min, max] per tier

data_fields.name: guard_amount_jitter_ratio
data_fields.donor_constant: x uniform [0.75, 1.25] when amount >= 4 (candidate stacks only)

data_fields.name: hidden_road_penalty_ratio
data_fields.donor_constant: score divided by 10 when the guard hides a road

best_idea: A reward's guard strength is a two-term hinge curve of the reward value with a per-tier row, the guard is the creature whose AI value fits that strength, and its count is the strength divided by that AI value.
decision_why: Keep the strength formula, the candidate-fit rule and the count rule as authoring-time data (the tier row is picked by zone data, the fallback is a named field); reject the generator's random placement and its retry loop, which Frankendom does not need at play time.
acceptance: An authoring test: a pile of value 6000 in a normal zone on a normal map gives strength 5000, a guard is required, the stack amount is 5000 divided by the creature's AI value, jittered to 75 to 125 percent only when the amount is 4 or more, and a pile at or below the tier threshold gets no guard.
